title: Overload Shutdown
shortDescription: Brushless RIDGID tool current-limited to protect motor.
fullDescription:
RIDGID 18V Octane and Max Output tools use electronic overload protection. E01 triggers when sustained current exceeds the motor rating — typically after a bit binds or the tool is used beyond its capacity.

Restart requires a trigger release of at least 3 seconds.

fixSteps.title: Clear bind
fixSteps.instruction: Back bit out and inspect for damage/dullness.

whenToCallPro: If overloads happen on light work, register warranty service through Lifetime Service Agreement.

faq.a: Yes — registered tools carry RIDGID's Lifetime Service Agreement.

title: Thermal Cut-Out
shortDescription: Tool overheated — cool-down required before restart.
fullDescription: Internal thermistor detects winding or driver temperature over 85 °C and kills power. Allow 15-20 minutes cool-down in ambient air.

fixSteps.title: Cool down
fixSteps.instruction: Place tool in shade for 20 minutes.

whenToCallPro: If overheating happens without heavy load, LSA warranty service.

faq.a: 15-20 minutes in ambient; longer if in direct sun.

title: Battery Low Voltage
shortDescription: Battery voltage sags below cut-off under load.
fullDescription: Older 18V Hyper-Lithium packs hit low-voltage cut-off when cells age. E03 protects cells from over-discharge.

fixSteps.title: Swap pack
fixSteps.instruction: Use a fully charged Max Output pack.

fixSteps.title: Warranty
fixSteps.instruction: If pack is <3 years old and registered, LSA covers replacement.

whenToCallPro: N/A — register pack with RIDGID for LSA.

faq.q: How long should a pack last?
faq.a: 3-5 years of daily use; LSA covers longer.

title: Battery Not Recognized
shortDescription: Tool cannot communicate with the battery.
fullDescription: RIDGID battery data pin communicates cell temp and SOC. E04 means terminals are dirty or the pack BMS has failed.
symptoms: Tool flashes on attach, no run

fixSteps.title: Clean terminals
fixSteps.instruction: Spray with electrical contact cleaner and dry.

fixSteps.title: Try other pack
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm whether the fault is the pack or the tool.

whenToCallPro: LSA replacement if pack is faulty.
videoSearchQuery: RIDGID battery not recognized clean terminals

faq.a: Not officially. Use LSA for warranty exchange.

title: Trigger Fault
fullDescription: Dust infiltration into the trigger assembly is the #1 cause. Cleaning usually restores operation.

faq.a: None — dust + lube = paste. Dry air only.

title: Motor Commutation Fault
shortDescription: Brushless motor will not spin — hall or driver failure.
fullDescription: Severe E06 means the BLDC driver cannot sense motor position. Usually water ingress or MOSFET failure. Send for service.

fixSteps.title: Isolate fault
fixSteps.instruction: Test with known-good pack; if tool still won't run, motor/driver is at fault.

fixSteps.title: LSA service
fixSteps.instruction: Ship to RIDGID authorized service center.

whenToCallPro: Always — LSA covers parts/labor for registered tools.

faq.a: Register tool online within 90 days of purchase; keep receipt.

title: Chuck Slip
shortDescription: Bit slipping in chuck under load.
fullDescription: Worn chuck jaws or bit shank. Replace chuck with OEM.

fixSteps.title: Replace chuck
fixSteps.instruction: Remove retention screw (LH thread), unscrew chuck.

faq.a: Yes — one screw and a firm pull.

title: Charger Fault
fullDescription: RIDGID chargers signal fault with flashing red/green. Pack temperature out of range, cell fault, or charger defect.

fixSteps.title: Condition pack
fixSteps.instruction: Warm/cool pack to room temp, retry.

fixSteps.title: Try another charger
fixSteps.instruction: Test pack on a known-good RIDGID charger.

whenToCallPro: LSA if fault persists with known-good pack.

faq.q: Can I leave packs on the charger?
faq.a: Yes — maintenance mode keeps the pack topped off.

title: Work Light Failure
shortDescription: Onboard LED work light not functioning.
fullDescription: LED work lights are driven by a dedicated circuit on the control board. E09 logs when the light fails to illuminate on trigger.

fixSteps.title: LSA service
fixSteps.instruction: Under LSA, RIDGID replaces the control board.

whenToCallPro: LSA path — usually free on registered tools.

faq.a: Yes — the work light is cosmetic for function.

title: Direction Switch Fault
fullDescription: The direction selector must be fully in forward or reverse; center position is safety lock. E10 covers dirty or broken selector circuits.

fixSteps.title: Push selector full travel
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm forward or reverse fully selected.

faq.a: Prevents accidental trigger activation during carry/storage.
